I farm in Quzhou County, so at the start of the year I will keep to the pattern I know best and trust most: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. I am 60 years old and I do not want a risky or complicated crop plan that needs too much labor, too much market guessing, or too much technical management. Wheat and maize fit my local weather, my soil, my habit of work, and the tools I can use. I will use improved seed because I want steady yield and better resistance, but I will not make the management too heavy. For wheat, I will use moderate fertilizer, water it a few times at key stages, and control weeds and disease with limited spraying. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize, use a little more nitrogen for stronger growth, give fewer irrigations because of summer rain if it comes, and spray only when pests or disease pressure are clear. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing every season and still prepares the land well enough. My goal is stable grain for income and low enough risk that I can manage the whole year myself.
